title: Explainable temporal machine learning of multimorbidity trajectories after acute myocardial infarction: complementing clinical risk scores with mechanistic phenotypes
journal: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association
source_type: retrospective cohort study with temporal clustering, supervised machine learning, survival analysis, and genetic/pathway analyses
source_internal_consistency_notes: Figure 1 schematic reports CatBoost as best with AUC-ROC 0.77 and weighted accuracy 65%, while the Results text and Figure 3 report XGBoost as highest-discrimination (AUC-ROC 0.906) and CatBoost AUC-ROC 0.900 with weighted accuracy 77.3%. Conflicting figure values were preserved as separate source-reported atoms and tagged source_internal_conflict.
Figure 1 depicts the pre-AMI window as -365 to 0 days; Methods text defines the primary window as 365 to 1 day before AMI and the sensitivity window as 365 to 7 days before AMI.

Results prose reports median age at AMI 69 years (IQR 63-74), while Table 1 reports Age 62.0 (56.0, 66.0) without specifying the time reference in the row; this may reflect baseline versus AMI age but is not resolved in the supplied main-text PDF.
extraction_limitations: Supplementary tables/figures referenced in the article (including Table S2, Tables S1/S3/S4/S5 and Figures S1-S3) were not included in the supplied 10-page main-text PDF, so supplement-only assertions were not extracted.
No external web verification was used; extraction is grounded only in the supplied paper and the project atom schema/validators.

The atom schema requires exposure context for quantitative_result atoms; descriptive cohort statements without a natural exposure were represented as population_description atoms rather than inventing an exposure.
All atoms are marked needs_review because extraction was performed by a language model and no human verification step was supplied.
